items.source: PR #156 review finding M2, Local Daemon design steward adjudication, and campaign disposition request

evidence.details: Both operator policies, the reviewed credential-local mechanism, and the Windows job-terminal receipt are selected. Campaign accepted the runtime-independent native owner, registry, admission, I/O, cancellation and publication, platform receipt, join, failure-hold, and shutdown design, including C=2 and B=3s as unmeasured engineering limits. The operator later selected the Windows receipt's explicit residual limits, and the same worker now has autonomous ordinary solution and implementation authority. These decisions are not implementation correctness, runtime proof, M2 completion, merge, or release.

decisionHistory.selectedDisposition: Route to an operator-owned policy decision. No remedy, contract narrowing, or Unix escape-coverage waiver is selected, and the native-worker prototype is not accepted. General autonomy does not authorize any of these choices.
decisionHistory.dispositionAuthority: Campaign e06813c4-1db2-4d77-b8d3-3addc6a1824c requested this hold; the policy decision belongs to the operator, who has not made it. This entry records a pending, unselected decision, not an accepted remedy.

decisionHistory.question: May Telex define --password-command as a one-shot invocation, cleaning up its owned in-scope helpers on completion or cancellation and explicitly excluding intentionally persistent, escaped, or broker-launched background work from this command's supported lifecycle contract?

For normal Telex host shutdown, may credential cleanup add up to 3 seconds after logical command/Wait completion, with admission closed and owned workers drained/joined; if receipt is still missing at that bound, should Telex report cleanup failure and retain ownership rather than report a clean exit?
decisionHistory.exactChoice: Approve bounded orderly-exit drain and explicit failure hold (Recommended)

decisionHistory.priorState: The mechanism and numeric targets were conditional and unaccepted before this decision; earlier decision-history entries and proposal commits remain historical snapshots.
decisionHistory.acceptedScope: The exact reviewed credential-local native owner, registry, finite admission, C=2 aggregate occupied slots, same-source barrier, owned nonblocking I/O, atomic cancellation and publication, B=3s internal cleanup-observation target, platform receipt, join, failure-hold, and shutdown design with every stated condition and limit.
decisionHistory.limits: The accepted numeric limits are not measured performance or universal finite OS guarantees. Product writes, runtime proof, M2 closure, thread resolution, merge, and release remain unauthorized.

decisionHistory.note: Campaign authorized the exact four-blob atomic landing, and the Local orchestrator independently verified it. The installed blobs kept recommendation-time fields, including landingAuthorized false; this entry and currentAuthority resolve landing only.

decisionHistory.acknowledgement: The same worker acknowledged the standalone grant before editing at 2e2f3b99 and began the accepted plan phases P1-P7.
decisionHistory.scope: Complete bounded P1-P7 implementation and proof in original PR #156, including the narrow existing console owning-host drain. The original M1, C1, and C2 commits and PAW history are preserved. The intentionally red credential regression may become an actual regression while its original negative evidence is retained.
decisionHistory.limits: Permission and phase progress only. M2 is not implemented, measured, runtime-proven, reviewed, or merged; merge and release are not authorized.

decisionHistory.question: May I adopt the explicit Windows job-terminal completion contract described above, accepting its residual kernel/driver/I/O limitations instead of requiring every former descendant process handle to be signaled before completion?
decisionHistory.exactChoice: Approve Windows job-terminal completion with the documented limits (Recommended)
decisionHistory.meaning: Select the checked exact-job termination, zero active accounting, exact launched-leader signaling, checked owned I/O and handle finalization, and native join conjunction before eligible atomic publication and source/admission release. Former descendant handles may remain nonsignaled during residual rundown; the choice does not establish a universal user-mode, memory, kernel, driver, external-I/O, reference-lifetime, or finite residual-resource fence.

conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.scope: Credential-specific process-local admission and ownership registry shared across password-command calls and Tokio runtimes in one host, not a global service or general process manager.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.cleanupObservationBasis: The proposed three seconds reuses the existing recovery grace and is not a measured OS reap guarantee.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.admission: Count setup, running, output collection, cancellation, completed-but-unjoined work, and FAILED_HELD through ownership discharge. Retain the same-source barrier through cleanup. A queued caller uses its existing budget, launches no native work before admission, and does not enter an internal payload queue. Capacity pressure is not bad credentials and does not reset clocks.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.ownership: The native owner retains process scope, stdout and stderr pipes, cancellation, result publication, cleanup receipt, and thread completion independently of Tokio. Cancellation and result publication are atomic.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.output: Use nonblocking owned readers with no detached readers, partial credential publication, or new truncation policy. Preserve environment, working directory, shell parsing, complete UTF-8 trim, and nonzero behavior. Sanitize diagnostics.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.failure: Cleanup observation timeout or failure enters FAILED_HELD and retains the exact invocation registry record: slot, source reservation, owned Windows process and job handles or Unix unreaped leader, pipes, and worker-thread obligation. The owning host retains the record, closes affected admission, and reports a sanitized failure naming the obligation. It is not a cleanup receipt and does not authorize automatic restart, discarded ownership, a hidden forever worker, or a replacement cleanup queue. Permanently holding every ordinary Unix completion is not an adequate implementation.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.platform: Windows requires a private noninheritable job, documented process and primary-thread handles, suspended create and assign-before-resume, no breakaway fallback, explicit setup-failure cleanup, and observed process, zero-active-job, reader, and thread completion. Unix requires pre-exec group setup, the sole unreaped leader through the last signal, exact child reap, and no cached-PGID signal after reap, subreaper, global wait, process scan, or escaped-process action.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.unixReceipt: Establish a dedicated group before exec, retain the exclusive waitable unreaped leader through every mutating group signal, send the final signal while the anchor is valid, irreversibly revoke further signal authority, reap the exact leader, and use the former PGID only as a read-only observation key. Receipt requires conclusive platform absence, exact leader reap, completed or closed owned I/O, and native completion and join. Presence, denial, ambiguity, possible reuse, or errors retain the cleanup obligation without signal authority.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.platformProof: Execute real Windows and every claimed supported Unix target, including Linux and macOS if both remain supported. Compile-only or skipped runtime coverage is insufficient.

postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.historicalDisposition: Superseded by unixReceiptRecommendation after the single bounded API-level follow-up; retained for chronology and not the current technical recommendation.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.scope: Ordinary non-escaped Unix helpers, separate from intentionally escaped, persistent, or broker-created work.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.requiredProductionSequence: For each claimed Unix target, name the stable owned object, member-completion observation excluding the identity anchor, last signal, nonconsuming observation where needed, exact leader reap, identity release, and error behavior.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.forbiddenApproaches: Do not use PID, name, or ancestry scans, unrelated waits, a subreaper, global manager, cgroup, or coverage waiver.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.proofBoundary: Production API feasibility is required before implementation. Real-helper tests later corroborate implementation correctness and do not replace the production completion definition.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.notImpossibilityProof: No supported complete sequence has yet been supplied or justified. This does not assert that no platform-specific solution exists.

unixReceiptRecommendation.verdict: design-recommendation-ready; technically feasible with supported-API conditions
unixReceiptRecommendation.supersedes: The earlier blanket Unix ordinary-helper receipt feasibility blocker, but not its chronology.
unixReceiptRecommendation.groupLifetime: An ordinary non-escaped member keeps the original process group extant after leader reap, and reparenting does not erase its group membership. Conclusive later absence proves the original group ended. Later numeric reuse may produce conservative presence or error holds but cannot restore that group or confer signaling authority.
ordering: Establish a dedicated group before exec with leader PID equal to PGID and greater than one.
Retain exclusive waitable unreaped leader ownership through every mutating group signal; nonconsuming leader observation may be used.
Send the last termination signal while the identity anchor is valid, then irreversibly enter a no-more-group-signals state.
Observe and reap only the exact owned leader; ECHILD or competing reaping is an ownership error, not receipt.
After reap, use the former PGID only as a read-only observation key within the existing cleanup budget and never send it another nonzero signal.
Require exact leader reap, conclusive group absence, completed or closed owned I/O, and native completion and join before receipt and admission release.

linux.query: getpriority(PRIO_PGRP, P), never setpriority; clear thread-local errno before each call.
linux.absence: Only return -1 with errno ESRCH is conclusive absence.
linux.presence: Any successful result is presence, including nice value -1 with errno zero.
linux.inconclusive: EINTR permits read-only retry within the same budget. EPERM, EACCES, EINVAL, ENOSYS, unexpected errors, unknown context, or known ESRCH-fabricating sandbox or interposer behavior are not absence.
linux.limit: Require the native PID namespace and supported syscall semantics. Do not claim universal result-fabrication detection or use Linux kill(-P, 0) as the absence predicate.

macos.query: Supported libc POSIX/UNIX03 kill(-P, 0), not a private raw syscall or legacy non-POSIX variant.
macos.absence: Return -1 with ESRCH is conclusive absence under the supported POSIX-mode semantics.
macos.presenceOrInconclusive: Return zero is presence. EPERM, including unsignalable, MAC-denied, or zombie-only cases, is not absence.
macos.bindingProof: Implementation review and genuine runtime tests must verify the actual libc binding and supported-target conformance. Do not generalize the Linux getpriority predicate to macOS.

unixReceiptRecommendation.errorsAndRaces: Final SIGKILL failure, partial delivery, changed permissions, missed concurrent forks, surviving ordinary helpers, zombies, reparenting, or slow adopter reaping prevent receipt or retain a conservative hold. Telex reaps only its exact child and sends no post-reap catch-up signal.
unixReceiptRecommendation.failedHeld: After reap, FAILED_HELD retains the exact invocation record, slot, source reservation, responsible host, observation key, pipes, and native thread obligation, but no signal authority. It reports sanitized failure and permits no automatic restart, ownership discard, growing retry queue, or clean-exit claim.
unixReceiptRecommendation.proofBoundary: Campaign accepted this intended design. Product implementation and genuine Windows, Linux, and macOS runtime proof remain pending; existing tests are not proof of the new mechanism.

operatorShutdownDecision.choiceSelected: Approve bounded orderly-exit drain and explicit failure hold (Recommended)
operatorShutdownDecision.approvedScope: Preserve logical command and Wait result deadlines. Normal exit of the host that owns credential work may take up to three additional seconds to close admission and drain and join owned workers concurrently against one absolute current cleanup budget.
operatorShutdownDecision.budgetLimits: Do not renew the budget per worker or multiply it by capacity. Waiting three seconds is not a cleanup receipt.
operatorShutdownDecision.missingReceipt: Report cleanup failure and retain named ownership and escalation, potentially beyond three seconds. Do not report clean exit or promise an unconditional three-second OS process-exit bound.
operatorShutdownDecision.ownershipLimit: Only the host owning credential work drains it. A client does not drain remote-host work, and Telex does not own preexisting external agents or broker-created work.
operatorShutdownDecision.notApproved: Measured performance, a universal finite OS cleanup guarantee, product implementation, runtime correctness proof, M2 completion, product writes, thread resolution, merge, and release remain unapproved.

evidence.evidenceLevel: Worker-supplied runtime evidence. The Local orchestrator verified all eight frozen artifact hashes, and the reconciler rechecked the packet index and checkpoint hashes. No one reran the tests or established source-to-binary exactness.
evidence.insidePollCleanup: After helper readiness and verified membership in the private invocation job, inside poll_cleanup immediately before it would return true, the retained leader handle was signaled and a successful accounting query reported ActiveProcesses 0, while the retained helper process handle with SYNCHRONIZE rights returned WAIT_TIMEOUT (258). In an isolated diagnostic the helper signaled about 1.4766 ms later without a second kill or fallback; that is not a maximum or acceptable delay. The assertion stops before return, so this does not show that the execution emitted a receipt or released admission.
evidence.afterRelease: Separate parent capacity and repeated-cancellation cases observed an unsignaled retained helper or shell handle after native-owner join, cleaned-scope drop including kill-on-close job closure, and registry removal. They did not record which process index failed or the later signal delay, and do not independently establish the membership or lag seen inside poll_cleanup.
evidence.results: Stronger module suite 7 passed, 3 failed, 1 child-only entry ignored; isolated diagnostic red; parent target 5 passed, 2 failed. Earlier green finite and grace cases polled both conditions and did not establish ordering.
evidence.provenanceLimit: Hashes freeze post-run artifacts only; no contemporaneous source-tree or executable digest was captured. Some raw API values, complete accounting buffers, per-operation timestamps, test PE architecture, and every member's final independent signaling are unrecorded.

stewardDocumentaryVerdict.conclusion: No documented guarantee was established that successful ActiveProcesses-zero accounting is ordered after every former member process object becomes signaled. consolidatedAdjudication.frozenCodeAssessment: The displayed code uses an explicit owned invocation job with checked assignment before resume, checks the accounting query result before reading it, uses a source-consistent x64 accounting layout, distinguishes wait results, and retains a SYNCHRONIZE-capable helper handle with verified job membership and no shown close or reopen. No wrong-job, failed or default-zero query, ABI or layout, wait-return, or handle-lifetime error was identified that explains away the report.
consolidatedAdjudication.evidenceSeparation: The A assertion runs before poll_cleanup returns true and is not itself a receipt or publication. B observes retained handles after join, cleaned-scope and job-handle drop, and record removal, and does not identify the failing role, job membership, or lag. Post-run snapshots cannot certify the originally compiled bytes.
consolidatedAdjudication.conclusion: Job accounting reaching zero is not a documented fence for completion of every member. No complete supported stronger production sequence is justified yet. This is not an impossibility, kernel-cause, continued-user-code, or harm claim, and it grants no new supervision machinery.
consolidatedAdjudication.remainingRequirement: A supported invocation-local completion barrier, or complete lifetime-safe member-handle ownership and observation covering all ordinary scoped descendants, including concurrent and short-lived ones, before receipt and admission release.

finalDebugCandidateAssessment.verdict: design-feasibility-blocked; candidate not accepted within current scope
finalDebugCandidateAssessment.documentedPerProcessFence: For a process in the debugging chain, Windows documents a per-process fence: keep an authorized duplicate of its CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT process handle, continue its EXIT_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT, then wait for the duplicate to signal.
finalDebugCandidateAssessment.inventoryGap: DEBUG_PROCESS inheritance stops when another process in the chain is created with DEBUG_PROCESS. An ordinary child can start a new debugging chain while staying in the private job, which is not necessarily job escape, persistent background work, or broker creation. The accepted exclusions therefore do not make the debug inventory equal the job scope, and root exit, empty known handles, event-wait timeout, or job accounting zero do not prove complete inventory.
finalDebugCandidateAssessment.materialSemantics: Debugger-visible behavior is materially new semantics: tools can detect a debugger, debug events suspend processes until continued, and event, handle, continuation, and thread-ownership obligations are added. Approving that behavior alone would not close the inventory gap.
finalDebugCandidateAssessment.limits: No supported replacement is accepted. Not a general Windows impossibility claim or a runtime claim. No debug experiment, new agent, or source work was performed.

items.source: PR #156 M2 Unix platform delegate source analysis, with existing design steward interpretation

evidence.evidenceLevel: Source-only prediction. No macOS program was run, and all Linux and macOS runtime proof remains unrun. Only cross-target cargo check and clippy for x86_64-apple-darwin were reported.
evidence.details: In pinned XNU, process-group signaling skips zombies and POSIX behavior returns EPERM when no member is signalable. The frozen Unix implementation sends a mandatory final group SIGKILL while the leader is still unreaped, and returns any nonzero signal error, including EPERM, as cleanup failure. If ordinary successful completion leaves only the unreaped leader zombie, that signal could fail and hold an otherwise finished invocation, conflicting with the requirement that ordinary completions not remain permanently held.
evidence.stewardInterpretation: The steward reads the pinned zombie filtering and UNIX03 EPERM behavior as applying to the final SIGKILL, and recommends only that the anchored attempt result stay separate from the independent later receipt: record the attempt, seal signals, reap the exact leader, then require the full read-only absence, I/O, and join conjunction. The correction hold remains while campaign classifies authority.

consolidatedAdjudication.frozenCodeAssessment: The frozen Unix cleanup sends the final signal, seals further signals, and then propagates any nonzero SIGKILL error, including EPERM, as failure. That result is latched before the exact child reap and the post-reap observation, and the common owner then records the scope as failed and held, so the path cannot reach the independent receipt.
consolidatedAdjudication.conclusion: Because pinned XNU returns EPERM for a zombie-only group on a nonzero signal, this is a concrete conditional source defect in ordinary leaf completion. It is not an executed macOS failure or pass.
consolidatedAdjudication.proposedCorrection: For the justified macOS final-attempt EPERM case only: keep the error as attempt evidence, irreversibly seal signals, then proceed with bounded exact-owned leader reap and the independent post-reap absence, I/O, and join predicate. Post-reap EPERM stays Present, never absence. Ownership, setup, ECHILD, ABI, reap, and query failures are never ignored, and cancellation or command errors never become credential success.

campaignCorrectionAuthorization.classification: Ordinary implementation correction of the already-accepted independent receipt ordering, limited to the justified macOS final nonzero-signal EPERM path. Not a new predicate or policy.
campaignCorrectionAuthorization.authorizedImplementers: Lead worker 38d183fb-df5d-4e65-88f3-e27b62e3c92f with existing Unix delegate 32add9eb-9543-42bf-808c-7d6e34d032f3.

campaignCorrectionAuthorization.prohibited: EPERM is never absence or a successful kill, and post-reap EPERM means Present. Setup, identity, ECHILD, ABI, reap, and query errors are never ignored. No new privilege, post-reap kill, renewed budget, or partial credential. Other error, cancellation, and output rules are unchanged. Anything beyond this exact path requires a stop and reviewed Tier B reconciliation.

field.body:
## Field report: #166 repair merged (PR #196, main 8d7815a8)

PR #196 merged at 8d7815a8d0fb8c6f465d441904044bd20f7dcc7b (gated head 9b538e4f, tree 220cdcfa, CI run 40264045091 attempt 1, 21/21 success, no retry or waiver). Gate record: https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/pull/196#issuecomment-6416830413

### Consequence

- The repair is a dependency floor, not a Telex code change. Cargo.lock moves Mio 1.2.1 to 1.2.4 (only the mio package changed, plus the direct mio edge). The Windows target table in Cargo.toml now requires `mio ^1.2.4` and `tokio ^1.39.1` (both default-features = false), so downstream consumers cannot resolve the older Tokio route that wraps Mio 0.8 beside the fixed Mio. No production Rust source changed.
- What was fixed: the Mio defect that hosted evidence reached directly (Mio 1.2.1 `write_done` panic, `State::None => unreachable!()`, named_pipe.rs:969, run 40254795271, locked job 121354231731). Upstream tokio-rs/mio#2014 (in 1.2.4) keeps a submitted overlapped read/write from reporting Err, which otherwise leaves the completion without its reserved Arc. The same workload on 1.2.4 ran 3 x 400,000 rounds clean (job 121354231722, artifact 12622392155).
- What is NOT claimed: no native stack maps any of the six observed Telex failures to this defect. A clean run is not proof of absence; the upstream race tests include randomized loops. The operator authorized this as the repair with the condition that a repeat native crash reopens #166. It does.
- CI changes: the diagnostic experiment jobs (named-pipe race, targeted stress) were removed. Retained: ordinary-job postmortem dump capture and `windows-heap-diagnostics`. Added in Feature combinations: a step that checks a single Mio 1.2.4 resolves for the repo and the defaults-disabled consumer fixture, and a step that requires Tokio 1.38.2 to be rejected with the specific Tokio floor conflict.
- Corrections to the PR body (it was the source of truth at merge, so recording them here): the line saying #203 and #204 must be cleared before the gate is stale. Campaign ruled #203 separate (it is tracked on its own, PR #207); #204 was closed via PR #205 before this gate. The test-isolation environment additions in the retained capture are also not described in the body.

### Deferred work (gate debts 1-8 from the gate record)

These are deferred, non-blocking, and I have not filed separate issues for them; they are listed so Campaign can route them.

1. ProcDump is downloaded on every hosted run and verified only by Authenticode signature, with no hash pin; required Windows jobs depend on Sysinternals being available.
2. When dumps exist, analysis downloads the Windows SDK and public symbols. Cost only on failing runs.
3. The negative Tokio step depends on the live crates.io index and Cargo's resolver wording. It fails closed, so the failure mode is noise, not a silent pass.
4. The capture tests check text only, and the floor test pins exactly 1.2.4, so a future Mio bump also needs a test edit.
5. The floor applies only on Windows (by design).
6. Dump capture is proven for 0xc0000005 only. Capture of 0xc0000409 and 0xc0000374 is unproven: those aborts produced no dump through AeDebug or WER LocalDumps.
7. The two PR-body issues described above (stale #203/#204 line; undocumented test-isolation env additions).
8. Record the Windows Tokio 1.39.1+ requirement in the next release notes.

### Discoveries and dispositions

| Discovery | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Four original 0xc0000005 failing artifacts (status hint, concurrent first use, destructor drain, PR194 busy-station status child) | Preserved by immutable artifact ID with a manifest; kept as history, not re-run. |
| Observation 5 (PR202 first use, run 40230509989 attempt 2, 0xc0000374, artifact 12613228369) and observation 6 (main faf4f883, run 40260369255, job 121371242766, 0xc0000374, artifact 12624059243; failed in the selected predecessor's initial attach, before intent seeding or the upgrade) | Retained as history under #166, deduplicated by run/job. Observation 6 ran on a lock still at Mio 1.2.1. No common cause or fault location established; artifact 12624059243 contents not inspected. |
| Mio 1.2.1 `write_done` State::None panic reached on a hosted runner | Repaired by the Mio 1.2.4 floor and lock (this PR). Submitted-I/O/Arc explanation remains a hypothesis for the Telex observations. |
| Clean experiments (targeted stress 40/40 under full PageHeap, artifact 12622123576; 3 x 400k on 1.2.1 and 1.2.4) | Kept as history; explicitly not evidence of absence. |
| Tokio before 1.39.1 wraps Mio ^0.8.9, so a defaults-disabled consumer could carry that route beside the new Mio floor (design finding DI-196-01) | Fixed: Windows `tokio ^1.39.1` floor, release-contract assertion, and a CI step requiring Tokio 1.38.2 to be rejected. Evidence is crates.io dependency metadata (1.38.2: Mio ^0.8.9; 1.39.1 onward: Mio ^1.0.1; 1.39.0 yanked), not a compiled reproducer. |
| The first negative check passed on any resolver failure (DI-196-02) | Fixed: it now requires all three expected Tokio conflict fragments and fails on success or any other error. |
| Watcher library-harness 0xc0000409 (run 40254795271, job 121354231596; log shows 60 announced, 37 ok, 1 ignored, no named failing test) | Routed to #203, not a #166 case. #203 owner reports a double panic during unwinding in watcher test fixtures, not Mio; fix is PR #207. |
| ForeignDaemon job failure | Routed to #204; closed via PR #205 before this gate. |
| #203 owner's hosted shard on Mio 1.2.1 hit the mio#2014 symptom in the watcher harness (`client::reconcile` -> `read_json_line`, BROKEN_PIPE, then 0xc0000005) | Recorded as reported evidence only. It shows the defect is reachable from a Telex-adjacent harness on 1.2.1; it does not map any of the six observations. Mio 1.2.4 addresses it; #207 does not. |
| Capture gap for 0xc0000409 and 0xc0000374 | Disclosed in the PR; not solved (debt 6). |
| Mio 1.2.1 to 1.2.4 also includes non-Windows changes (poll, UDS, kqueue, FreeBSD, Haiku) | Not treated as zero-risk; Linux/macOS and feature-profile CI jobs all passed at the gated head. |
| Full-repo `clippy -D warnings` fails on the local Rust 1.98 toolchain in untouched files (tests/copilot_plugin.rs, tests/release_upgrade.rs, a lib test) | Out of scope; untouched and not filed. CI at the gated head was green. |

### Next

- Main CI for 8d7815a8 is running (CI run 40328433964, Docs run 40328433981); I will post the result as a follow-up.
- If any native crash recurs, #166 reopens. Preserve the run, job, artifact ID and any dump, and do not retry past the failure.

gate.fullBody:
Campaign merge gate: MERGE + debt (confidence high). No hard stop, no fork.

Head e11c56ce2eb9005edd81e42f77c4a5a571128a98, tree 1707ac6b. Base main 7e91a233; drift since merge base is .streamliner only.

Floor:
- CI: 21/21 green at the exact head (run 40258493286, attempt 1), including Windows Build and test and InstalledCurrent. No retry, rerun or waiver.
- Merge: merge-tree is clean against main and against open PRs #194, #196 and #202. 0 unresolved threads.
- Exact-head receipts: independent source review issuecomment-6406872345, and steward design inspection issuecomment-6406877057.
- Body: says Closes #204. Local independently confirmed this packet.

Hard stops: none. The change is next to peer authentication but doesn't relax it. Only an exit that can be proven becomes retryable NotRunning; access denied or an unclear state stays terminal ForeignDaemon. There are no new variants, no wire or schema changes, and no release or #203 surface.

Correctness: the fix matches the #204 trace (a killed predecessor whose pipe is still open), sending it into the existing bounded probe and spawn loops. The exit check is conservative about PID reuse and about the STILL_ACTIVE (259) exit code.

Debt:
1. The PR body has no consequence line (normal) and no "no discoveries" statement.
2. In a contrived same-user case, a squatter whose pipe-creating process has exited while another process still holds the pipe gets a bounded Timeout/Unavailable instead of ForeignDaemon. The peer is still refused, so only the diagnostic class gets worse.
3. Nothing forces the ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER branch or a connection during handle rundown. Watch Windows InstalledCurrent on main, and file a new item if it recurs.
4. The evidence that the test fails before the fix is from diagnostic head 4f133e02, not this head.

Follow-up: the #204 field report, and the #196 owner's confirmation that this clears #196's Windows required job.

Field report for #204 after merging PR #205 (owner session 0fda8afd-ccfa-4aba-bbf2-c625b09280da).

Merged commit on main: faf4f883631c7aaec057dde4beca36daa29d29dd. Reviewed PR head: e11c56ce2eb9005edd81e42f77c4a5a571128a98. Gate: https://github.com/lossyrob/telex/pull/205#issuecomment-6407030627

Main CI push run 40260369255, attempt 1, at faf4f883, concluded failure overall:
- InstalledCurrent Postgres process proofs (Windows), job 121371242830: success. The crash-reattach proof did not reproduce ForeignDaemon on this run.
- Build and test (windows-latest), job 121371242766: failure. The #204 regression test `daemon::platform::tests::windows_exited_pipe_server_is_not_a_foreign_daemon` passed there (lib 573 passed, 0 failed). The failing test is `station_intent_upgrade_runs_the_selected_successor_and_restores_push` (tests/daemon_process_sqlite.rs:518), which exited with native abnormal status 0xc0000374. That is the #166 / PR #196 native error family, not #204's ForeignDaemon signature. It is retained as-is; I will not retry, rerun or waive it, and #204 is not reopened. It is routed to Local and the #166 owner.
- The other 19 jobs succeeded. The Docs push run 40260369359 at faf4f883 also succeeded.
- Retained artifacts: windows-build-test-crash 12624059243, windows-heap-diagnostics 12623779867, released-v021-upgrade-proof 12624622245.

One green InstalledCurrent run is not proof that the race is gone. Before the fix, the race reproduced in about 3 of roughly 58 Windows jobs.

1. PR body consequence/discoveries lines: resolved. The body now states "Consequence: normal." and "No discoveries."
2. Retained. In a contrived same-user case, a squatter whose pipe-creating process has exited while another process still holds the pipe now gets a bounded Timeout/Unavailable instead of ForeignDaemon. The peer is still refused; only the diagnostic class is worse.
